hens_rule_text: Hens allowed only with an annual city permit from the Department of Health and Community Wellness; the code sets no numeric cap. Not allowed at multi-family houses or their yards.
permit_notes: Permit from the Director of Health and Community Wellness, $10 fee, expires every December 31, revocable for cause after notice and hearing. Some secondary sites mention neighbor consent and a 25-hen limit; neither appears in the code article.
setback_notes: No part of the coop or runway may be closer than 20 feet to the doors or windows of any premises occupied by people, for dwelling or business.
coop_rules: Birds must be confined in a house or coop with an enclosed runway, no running at large. Coop floor must be cement or other watertight material; runway unfloored. Clean at least weekly. No fowl inside any dwelling.
zoning_notes: Banned outright in multi-family houses and multi-family house yards. Zoning code not separately checked.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Newark Code Title VI, Ch. 6:2, Art. 4, Secs. 6:2-28 to 6:2-37

sources.name: Newark Code, Article 4 Rabbits and Fowl (eCode360)

research_notes: Read the full Article 4 text via an Internet Archive copy (April 2026) of the eCode360 page. The code has no hen count cap; the 25-hen figure and neighbor-consent requirement seen on secondary sites could not be confirmed and may be permit-office practice.
